## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the direct launcher (`omarchy launch firefox webapp`) behaves as described: flavor resolution (`--browser`, then `FIREFOX_FLAVOR`, then a Firefox-based xdg default, then `firefox`), URL normalization and http(s) validation, per-URL profile skeleton, and `--class`/`--name` window identity. The new commands dispatch correctly, `bin/omarchy commands --check` reports 459 commands, `bin-style-test.sh` passes, and the new test passes 14/14 on this head and fails on the base tree.

Three issues were found in the installer path and its integration with the existing web app pipeline.

### Installed entries corrupt percent-encoded URLs

`bin/omarchy-webapp-install-firefox` escapes only `\` and `"` in its custom Exec line. The base installer's `desktop_exec_arg` also turns `%` into `%%` (and escapes `` ` `` and `$`), as the Desktop Entry Exec rules require. `test/shell.d/webapp-install-escaping-test.sh` covers exactly this case for Chromium web apps. Omarchy starts entries through `gtk-launch`, and GLib treats an unescaped `%X` as a field code.

Launching the generated entries with `gio launch` (GLib 2.88.3, launcher in dry-run mode):

```text
Installed URL                      URL received at launch             Result
https://example.com/s?q=a%20b      https://example.com/s?q=a0b        wrong URL, new profile, class no longer matches StartupWMClass
https://example.com/%c3%a9         https://example.com/'<App Name>'39  refused ("must not contain whitespace"), app never opens
Base installer, same URLs          unchanged                          correct
```

**Impact:** any installed Firefox web app whose URL contains `%` opens the wrong page in a fresh, logged-out profile, or does not open at all.

**Suggested change:** build the URL argument with the same escaping as `desktop_exec_arg`, and add a `gio launch` case to `firefox-webapp-test.sh` modelled on `webapp-install-escaping-test.sh`.

### Apps installed for `firefox` follow the current default browser instead

For the `firefox` flavor (explicit or defaulted), the installer computes `StartupWMClass` with `--browser firefox` but writes the Exec line without `--browser`. At launch, the launcher resolves the flavor again from `FIREFOX_FLAVOR` or the xdg default.

```text
Install: omarchy webapp install firefox App https://youtube.com/ icon firefox
  StartupWMClass=FFWebApp-7207dff0      profile firefox-ssb/7207dff0
  Exec=omarchy-launch-firefox-webapp "https://youtube.com/"

Launch with xdg default zen.desktop    -> zen-browser, ZenWebApp-7207dff0, zen-ssb/7207dff0
Launch with FIREFOX_FLAVOR=librewolf   -> librewolf,  LWWebApp-7207dff0,  librewolf-ssb/7207dff0
```

Entries installed with `zen`, `librewolf`, `waterfox` or `floorp` keep `--browser <flavor>` and are not affected.

**Impact:** this hits the users the feature targets (a Firefox-based default that is not Firefox): the explicit `firefox` choice is ignored, the pre-created profile is unused, and the window never matches the entry's `StartupWMClass`. The new test uses a Chromium xdg default, so install-time and launch-time flavors always agree there.

**Suggested change:** always write `--browser <flavor>` into the Exec line, `firefox` included.

### Remove > Web App does not see Firefox web apps

The PR description says `omarchy-webapp-remove` keeps working, but every existing detector matches only `omarchy-launch-webapp` or `omarchy-webapp-handler`:

- `bin/omarchy-webapp-remove` (picker index)
- `bin/omarchy-webapp-remove-all`
- `bin/omarchy-remove-launcher-entry` (app launcher remove action)
- the `when` condition of Remove > Web App in `default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc`

**Verified** in an isolated run: the picker lists only Chromium web apps, the menu entry is hidden when only Firefox web apps exist, remove-all leaves Firefox entries in place, and the launcher remove action deletes the `.desktop` file but leaves the icon. Removal by explicit name (`omarchy-webapp-remove <Name>`) works. No path removes the per-URL profile under `~/.mozilla/<flavor>-ssb/`.

**Impact:** Firefox web apps cannot be removed through the documented menu (`manual/25-web-apps.md` says "go to Remove > Web App"), and profiles accumulate.

**Suggested change:** add `omarchy-launch-firefox-webapp` to those four patterns, and decide whether removal should delete the profile (Linux Mint's Web App Manager does).

### Smaller notes

**Links that open a new tab (source only, not run):** the profile CSS hides `#TabsToolbar` and `#nav-bar` with `display: none`, and `user.js` leaves `browser.link.open_newwindow` at Firefox's default of 3 (new tab). A `target=_blank` link or plain `window.open` then opens a tab inside the web app window with no visible tab strip. Linux Mint's profile sets `browser.link.open_newwindow` to 2 and auto-hides the toolbox instead. This was not observed in a running browser.

**Documentation:** the new manual section says `omarchy webapp install firefox` "asks for" name, URL, icon and browser, but without arguments it prints usage and exits 1. The metadata `# omarchy:args=[name url icon [flavor [mime-types]]]` marks every argument optional, so `omarchy webapp install firefox` runs the binary instead of showing help; `<name> <url> <icon> [flavor] [mime-types]` would match the behavior. The examples use the name `YouTube`, which overwrites the stock `YouTube.desktop` and is replaced again by `omarchy-refresh-applications`.

**Side effect of validation:** the installer validates by calling the launcher with `DRY_RUN=1`, and the launcher creates the profile before its dry-run branch. A rejected install (for example a name containing `/`) still leaves a profile directory behind. Creating the profile only on a real launch would avoid this.

**Hyprland rules:** `default/hypr/apps/browser.lua` matches `([fF]irefox|zen|librewolf)`. None of the new classes (`FFWebApp-`, `ZenWebApp-`, `LWWebApp-`, `WFWebApp-`, `FloorpWebApp-`) matches, so these windows get the generic opacity rule rather than the browser rule (source only).

**`--no-remote`:** Firefox 131 and later ignore this flag. Web app URLs still do not reach a running main browser, because Firefox matches running instances by profile path, so only the code comment's stated reason is inaccurate.

**Optional (pre-existing):** `omarchy-launch-or-focus-firefox-webapp` joins its arguments into a string that `omarchy-launch-or-focus` runs through `eval`, so URLs containing `&`, `(`, quotes or `$(...)` are truncated, rejected with a syntax error, or partly executed. The existing `omarchy-launch-or-focus-webapp` behaves identically, and this PR wires no caller to the new wrapper. Building the string with `printf ' %q' "$@"` should keep the arguments literal in both wrappers (not tested).
